en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 16.1. Kusala-ttika, Hetu-duka The Positive-Negative Exposition of the Triplets and Couplets (Dhammānulomapaccanīya Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi): 16.1.
The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusala-ttika) and the Couplets on Roots (Hetu-duka)
The Tetrad of Conditions: Root Condition.
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root-condition, an unwholesome state that is not a root-condition arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root-condition, an unwholesome state that is not a root-condition arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root-condition, an indeterminate state that is not a root-condition arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root-condition...

Dependent on [a state that is] neither-unwholesome-nor-root and neither-indeterminate-nor-root, states that are neither-unwholesome-nor-root and neither-indeterminate-nor-root arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is a root, states that are neither-unwholesome-nor-root and neither-unwholesome-nor-root arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is a root, a state that is neither-unwholesome-nor-root arises by way of root-condition. An unwholesome...
Dependent on a root dhamma that is unwholesome, a dhamma that is neither wholesome nor a root arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a root dhamma that is unwholesome, a dhamma that is neither indeterminate nor a root arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a root dhamma that is unwholesome, dhammas that are both neither wholesome nor a root and neither indeterminate nor a root arise by way of root condition. Unwholesome...
Dependent on a root dhamma, unwholesome non-root and neither-wholesome-nor-unwholesome non-root dhammas arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate root dhamma, an unwholesome non-root dhamma arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate root dhamma, a neither-wholesome-nor-unwholesome non-root dhamma arises by way of root condition. Dependent on an indeterminate root...

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor a root, and neither unwholesome nor a root, states that are neither wholesome nor a root arise by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. [In the Positive Enumeration:
Thirteen in the root [condition], nine in the object [condition] ... pe ... three in the resultant [condition] ... pe ... thirteen in the non-disappearance [condition].
Negative Enumeration.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is not an object-condition and is a root-cause, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor a root-cause by way of the object-condition. (Abbreviated. Nine in the case of the not-object condition;

thirteen in the case of the not-predominance condition ... pe ... thirteen in the case of the not-prenascence condition ... pe ... nine in the case of the not-dissociation condition ... pe ... nine in the case of the not-disappearance condition.
(The sections on “Co-nascent” and “Associated” should also be expanded in the same manner as the section on “Dependent. Root-object:
A wholesome root-dhamma is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a not-wholesome, non-root dhamma. Wholesome...
A wholesome root-dhamma is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a dhamma that is neither unwholesome nor a root.
A wholesome root-dhamma is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a dhamma that is neither indeterminate nor a root.

A wholesome root-dhamma is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a dhamma that is neither unwholesome nor a root and for a dhamma that is neither indeterminate nor a root. [The wholesome root...]
A state that is neither wholesome nor a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither unwholesome nor a root.
An unwholesome state that is a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither unwholesome nor a root… five [answers].
A neutral state that is a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither wholesome nor a root… three [answers].
A wholesome root-dhamma is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome non-root dhamma. (Abbreviated. Under root: thirteen;
under object: eighteen; under predominance: fifteen; under proximity, contiguity, and conascence:
thirteen; under mutuality: nine; under dependence: thirteen; under strong-dependence: eighteen; under postnascence and repetition: [nine].
Nine; in the case of resultants, three; in the case of faculties and the path, eight; in the case of association and dissociation, nine ...
pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, thirteen. (The Chapter of Questions should be expanded.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is not a root-cause, there arises an unwholesome state that is neither unwholesome nor a root-cause, by way of root-condition. Dependent on a wholesome state that is not a root-cause, there arises an indeterminate state that is neither indeterminate nor a root-cause, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to cause: nine; with respect to object: nine ... pe ... with respect to result: three ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance: nine. (In all cases: nine.)
